memory_book_excerpt: I used to think family reunions were just polite small talk until the campfire the last night. Somebody pulled out a guitar and we sang until the fire went low. That is the version of this family I want to remember.

notes: Sister mentioned her father is in outpatient rehab; her mom has been under a lot of strain.
memory_book_excerpt: My dad came home from rehab this spring and we still don't really talk about it. Standing by the lake with him this weekend was the first time in a year it felt easy. I think my mom is finally sleeping again.

Cooking with grandma in the cabin kitchen was the best part of the whole trip. She speaks mostly Igbo and I speak mostly English but somehow we always got the jollof rice right. It was never the same twice and that is the whole point.

conflict_notes: Heated argument at the lake dinner Saturday about seating and old grievances; talked it through Sunday morning and it was resolved.
memory_book_excerpt: When my brother got deported, my mom stopped sleeping. I am the one who drives my little sister everywhere now. This reunion was the first weekend I got to just be a cousin again instead of the responsible one.

Last summer abuela taught me to make tamales from scratch and this weekend we did it again for the whole crowd. I learned that patience is its own ingredient. Watching everyone go quiet at the first bite was worth every hour on the corn husks.

notes: New ADHD diagnosis over the summer; medication adjustment in progress.
memory_book_excerpt: I got diagnosed with ADHD over the summer and the meds still make me feel a little strange some days. The lake was easier though — my head goes quiet near water. Skipping stones with the kids was the calmest I have felt in months.
My favorite moment was the poetry someone read around the fire. It felt like the way I actually think — short and sideways. I want to write something for next year's reunion
column13: but I don't have all the words for these feelings yet.

conflict_notes: A cousin's teasing at the group photo got under her skin; kept an eye on it the rest of the weekend.
notes: Was the target of a cousin's teasing; her therapist Dr. Kaur suggested journaling to work through it.
memory_book_excerpt: I started a journal this fall because Dr. Kaur said it might help. At first it was just dates and sad faces. By the reunion I was writing whole paragraphs
column12: and one of them was about how the lake at sunrise made me feel brand new.

memory_book_excerpt: My son and I are reading The Hobbit out loud together — one chapter every Sunday since the reunion campfire story night. He does all the dwarf voices and I do Bilbo. It takes us almost an hour because we keep laughing and starting over.

I used to dread reunions because my life feels messy right now. But everyone just made room for me. The morning I helped grandma flip pancakes and nobody asked a single hard question — that was the kindest thing anyone did all weekend.

conflict_notes: Argument during the drive up about who was hosting what; we do weekly check-in calls now and things are steadier.
memory_book_excerpt: I am working on being less short with people. Coach Miller from my running club said anger is just energy with nowhere to go, so I ran the lake trail every morning at the reunion. It helped. Sorry again for snapping in the car.

notes: Mother's cancer treatment ongoing; she is the primary caregiver. Extreme sensitivity around any health disclosures.
memory_book_excerpt: after my mom's mastectomy I helped with her drains and that was my whole autumn. Bringing her to the lake this weekend
column12: seeing her laugh with her sisters
column13: felt like a reward for all of it. She is okay now. I would write a whole book about her.

memory_book_excerpt: My speech therapist Ms. Levin has been teaching me to slow down so my words come out the way I mean them. At the reunion talent night I actually read a poem out loud in front of everyone. I am getting better and I am proud.

conflict_notes: Showed up late to two group activities; it read as flaky to some cousins but it is really a family logistics thing.
notes: Housing instability risk; mornings revolve around his autistic brother's routine. Lateness is family circumstance
memory_book_excerpt: not indifference.
column12: I know I missed the sunrise hike. Mornings are hard at my house because my little brother has autism and getting him out the door takes everything we have. I am not making excuses, just explaining. The afternoon by the lake made up for it.

conflict_notes: Long-standing rift; barely spoke this weekend and left early after a tense exchange.
notes: Vape/substance incident last fall; family started therapy. He is ashamed.
memory_book_excerpt: This reunion was hard for me. I made some choices last year I am not proud of. I have been talking to my mom more and we go to family therapy on Wednesdays now. Writing this down in the memory book is part of trying to do better.

I read on the dock every afternoon and finished three books over the long weekend. My favorite was A Wrinkle in Time. I am writing my own story about a girl who can hear what plants are thinking. It is going to be 200 pages.

My little cousin and I built a reading fort out of blankets and flashlights in the loft. We read Charlotte's Web together and I cried at the end even though I am supposed to be the grown-up. Caring about the story is a kind of bravery.

The lake was the only place all weekend where my brain went quiet. We swam out to the raft every afternoon and just floated. I keep telling people the reunion was relaxing and this is exactly what I mean.

notes: Recently relocated and still settling; going through a lot.
memory_book_excerpt: Everything in my life still feels temporary right now — new town, new routine, new everything. But sitting around the fire with all of you, I felt like I belonged to something steady for the first time in months.
Having all of my grandchildren in one kitchen again was the answer to a prayer. We rolled tamales
column12: we burned the first batch of pancakes
column13: and nobody minded. This is what I hoped for when I first dreamed up this reunion.

memory_book_excerpt: Cooking with the family this weekend reminded me that recipes are just instructions you can argue with. Grandma and I disagreed about the salt three times and both of us were right. I love that about this family.
People talk fast around the reunion table and I catch every third word. But out on the quiet dock at dusk
column13: I could finally keep up. Those slow talks were my favorite part.

memory_book_excerpt: Our old dog Scout got sick in January and we almost lost her
column12: so I nearly didn't come. Instead I brought her
column13: and watching her nap in the sun by the lake with the kids petting her was healing for both of us.

memory_book_excerpt: I filmed little clips of the whole weekend — the campfire
column13: grandma laughing. I am cutting them into a short movie for everyone. Turns out capturing a reunion is harder than it looks

memory_book_excerpt: The reunion fell right at the end of Ramadan this year
column12: so I broke my last few fasts with all of you at the lake. Explaining it to the little cousins over dinner
column13: instead of just quietly fasting alone
column14: made it feel like a celebration.

memory_book_excerpt: The quiet cabin porch was where I retreated when the crowd got to be too much. I used to think needing a break meant I was antisocial. This weekend I learned that stepping away and coming back is its own kind of belonging.

notes: Parents under financial stress; she has been translating bills at home. Watch for stress.
memory_book_excerpt: Money is tight at home and I carry more of it than a kid should. For one weekend at the lake, none of that followed me. I laughed so hard during the three-legged race that I forgot to worry, and I needed that more than anyone knew.
I tend to keep to myself at big gatherings because jumping in feels risky. This reunion
column12: my cousin just handed me a fishing rod and sat with me in silence for an hour. That mattered more than any speech.

memory_book_excerpt: I brought two rescue dogs from the shelter where I volunteer and they were the stars of the reunion. Watching the whole family fall in love with a scruffy pit bull named Rusty made my year. Animals do not care about anything but kindness.
Big loud group meals are the hardest part for me
column12: so I ate breakfast early on the quiet porch most mornings. Grandma always joined me. Those calm sunrise breakfasts with her were the reunion I will actually remember.

memory_book_excerpt: My grandma tells stories about crossing the border that I am only old enough now to understand. Hearing her tell them again by the fire
column13: I finally saw how much of this family she carried here herself.

notes: Family went through housing instability last fall and doubled up with relatives. He only recently opened up about it; handle gently.
memory_book_excerpt: Last fall was rough and I almost skipped the reunion out of pride. I am so glad I didn't. Nobody asked why my life looked different this year — they just made space for me at the lake and that was everything.
Big group toasts make my chest tight
column12: so instead of standing up to speak I wrote everyone a little note and left them on the pillows. Sharing my thanks that way
column14: felt like real growth for me.

memory_book_excerpt: I thought a whole weekend of family togetherness would drive me crazy until my grandfather showed me the little workshop at the cabin. We fixed the dock railing together without a single nail. Patience runs in this family and I am glad I got some of it.
I learned three ukulele chords over the winter and finally worked up the nerve to play at the campfire. It was shaky
column12: but the little cousins sang along anyway. Music is easier to share than feelings
column13: and this family sang loudest of all.

memory_book_excerpt: I am not much of a writer
column12: so leaving something in this memory book is hard for me. But I dictated most of it walking the lake trail and then cleaned it up. It probably still has mistakes. I care more that it sounds honest
